events.name: Data Salon: Context and Data
events.description:
An event series for fostering thought leadership across data disciplines and those who work closely with data practitioners, hosted by Newtown Analytics at Fractal Tech. This event will go beyond the hype and inspect the potential impact of AI on labor from well-informed business perspectives both on the ground and systemic.
MC'd by Akpanoluo Etteh, Sr. Director of Data Engineering at Arcspan (fmr: Anthropic, Bandcamp) and founder of The Soundshop music salon series, and co-hosted by Michael Bartoli, Founder of Newtown Analytics (fmr: obé Fitness)
Our featured collaborator: Omni
Omni is an AI analytics platform that gives every person and every AI agent the same governed definitions of the business's metrics. That puts Omni close to this month's question: what context does AI need before the business can trust its answers? Omni joins us through JD Costantini of their go-to-market team.
Bio: Began my career as a data engineering consultant at IBM working across industries and getting exposed to tons of different technologies across the data stack. After recognizing the innovation happening in the space, I moved into the AI Analytics startup space in 2021, and joined Omni 2 years ago. I love being able to work with clients of all shapes and sizes, finally delivering a trustworthy self-service analytics experience for the masses.
Presentation Teaser: We'll discuss how the marriage of context and data is the key to unlock the AI-era version of analytics. How data teams are evolving to be the stewards of semantics. Why you need to keep the business SMEs squarely in your feedback loop. And why collecting context is good, but optimizing how you use it is great.

events.name: Bible-plus-classics reading group returns(!!!) with Session 2.1: Creation and corruption
events.description:
Welcome back! / Start here!

At long last, we will resume our discussion group where we pair Bible passages with classic literature and philosophy. No beliefs required!
We will be kicking off Season Two at the very beginning with Genesis chapters 1-4, alongside a few other texts about new beginnings.
Our sessions will run for about 2 hours, with a break in the middle. These events are free of tuition, but you must own a physical Bible, and you will be required to purchase or borrow some more books as we go along.
Exact readings for this session
Please prepare by reading the excerpts described in the season doc under "Session 1: Creation and corruption". For this first session, the texts are all free online.
Altogether, these readings may take you up to about an hour:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IBA5ctBYNK-uiWrO3WCykldqZeRhrVXZd5QRaZ12DMU/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.bs12mvcmdjcg
More about "Season Two: Trials and Suffering"
In this second season, we’ll cover a variety of stories about trials and suffering. On the Bible side, there will be heavy doses of Genesis and Job, along with many other Old and New Testament episodes. From the wider canon, we’ll get perspectives from the likes of Borges, Oscar Wilde, Kierkegaard, Kafka, Simone Weil, Dostoevsky, Boethius, Nietzsche, Flannery O’Connor, and more. As a capstone, we will conclude with multiple sessions on Melville’s Moby-Dick.
This theme will last us through May 2027, with sessions roughly every other Wednesday.
Unlike in Season One, which served mainly as an introduction to the Bible itself, Season Two will lean more heavily on the “classics” half of our quest. The reading load will be heavier and more modern.
